body:
## Add Functions Downhill

Ordinary gradient descent adjusts numbers. Boosting adjusts the whole prediction function by adding a small new tree in the direction that lowers loss.

This view is called functional gradient descent. The loss supplies a desired correction at each training row, and the tree approximates that correction across feature space.

Second-order boosters also use local bend to scale corrections. Approximations, histogram bins, and distributed split summaries make this practical on large tables.
common_mistakes: Using a large learning rate and many deep trees without validation.
Treating library defaults as a substitute for leakage-safe evaluation.

real_world_usage: Boosted trees are among the strongest methods for structured tables.
